hook.text: Put this glass in the body and bone grows onto it — Larry Hench invented it in 1969 to help Vietnam veterans.

buildup.text: Bioglass 45S5 releases calcium and phosphate ions — forming a hydroxyapatite layer that bonds to living bone.

discovery.text: The ion release also stimulates genes in bone cells — bioglass doesn't just support bone, it signals cells to grow.

twist.text: Bioglass is too brittle for load-bearing use — but as a particulate or coating, it outperforms HA in bone bonding speed.

climax.text: Bioglass is FDA-approved for bone grafts and dental fillers — over a million patients treated since its invention.

punchline.text: A glass that talks to bone cells — materials science at its most alive.

quiz.question: What makes bioactive glass different from regular glass?
options: It is harder and more transparent
It releases ions that form hydroxyapatite and stimulate bone growth
It is flexible and won't shatter
